F53.quote: For years, we (me included) have cited without reading; but now the costs of that practice have become explicit. In other words, hallucinations expose the epistemic hygiene the legal profession has long lacked, and that is precisely why they deserve to be studied.

F54.quote: The use of generative AI by law firms for legal research resulted in the creation of the global "AI Hallucination Cases" database, in April 2025, established by HEC Paris and Sciences Po legal data analysis lecturer Damien Charlotin.
F54.claim: Wikipedia (Artificial intelligence): created April 2025 by Charlotin, HEC Paris and Sciences Po lecturer, as a result of law firms' use of generative AI

F55.quote: By 2026, judges had issued sanctions and bar associations had issued warnings due to attorney submissions to the courts containing fabricated case law citations hallucinated by AI tools.
F55.claim: Wikipedia (Artificial intelligence): by 2026 sanctions and bar warnings over AI-hallucinated citations

F56.quote: A database of incidents, "AI Hallucination Cases", was established in April 2025 by HEC Paris and Sciences Po legal data analysis lecturer Damien Charlotin; one year later, it listed over 1300 instances of hallucinations in legal decisions.
F56.claim: Wikipedia (Hallucination): established April 2025 by Charlotin; over 1,300 instances a year later

F57.quote: As of 14 June 2026, Canadian courts and tribunals have received at least 167 filings containing AI-hallucinated, fictitious citations, across 51 courts and tribunals.
F57.claim: Wikipedia (Hallucination), sourced to courtready.ca and the database's Canada filter: at least 167 Canadian filings by 14 June 2026

F58.quote: As of August 2026, Israeli courts and tribunals had identified at least 55 cases in which parties submitted documents containing fictitious citations or otherwise AI-hallucinated arguments.
F58.claim: Wikipedia (Hallucination), sourced to the database's Israel filter: at least 55 Israeli cases by August 2026

F59.quote: Due to the continued usage of GAI in the practice of law, Mata has been described as a landmark case by legal professionals,
F59.claim: Wikipedia (Mata v. Avianca), sourced to the database among others: Mata described as a landmark case
